newsitem.title: POLAND: POLISH BREWERS UP JAN-OCT SALES NINE PCT - REPORT.
newsitem.headline: POLISH BREWERS UP JAN-OCT SALES NINE PCT - REPORT.

text.p: Polish brewers sold nine percent more beer in the first 10 months of this year than in the same period in 1995, a report by the Piwochmiel research firm in the daily Rzeczpospolita said on Tuesday.

Polish brewers sold 14.3 million hectolitres of beer during the first 10 months. Leading vendor Elbrewery Company Ltd>sold 2.3 million hectolitres gaining a 16.2-percent market share, but upped sales by only 3.8 percent.

Lech Browary Wielkopolski SA>(Lech) and Browary Tyskie Gorny Slask SA> (Tychy)> showed the most dynamic growth lifting sales by 25.6 percent and 16.3 percent respectively. Earlier this year South African Breweries Ltd SABJ.J>(SAB) bought strategic stakes in the two brewers.
They sold 1.3 million hectolitres and 1.6 million hectolitres this year, the fourth and second largest sellers with 9.3-percent and 11.1-percent market shares respectively.

Zaklady Piwowarskie w Zywcu SA ZYWI.WA>(Zywiec) ZYWI.WA>, 31.8-percent owned by Heineken HEIN.AS>, was the third largest vendor, selling 1.5 million hectolitres and upping sales 15.2 percent to gain a 10.3-percent market share.

Fifth largest seller Okocimskie Zaklady Piwowarskie SA OKOC.WA> Okocim OKOC.WA>, 31.8-percent owned by Carlsberg CARCb.CO>, increased sales by 5.2 percent to 1.2 million zlotys to capture an 8.2-percent market share.
Poland's top-five brewers sell about half the country's beer. -- Warsaw Newsroom +48 22 653 9700
